title: Ordinance SDA/MAPA No. 1,699 of 4 November 2026. Updates the phytosanitary requirements for the importation of propagative material of gypsophila (Gypsophila spp.) from any origin and repeals the Ordinance SDA/MAPA No. 1,660 of 8 July 2026
description:
The main change introduced by the published Ordinance is the removal of Arion hortensis and Lygus elisus from the additional declarations required for imports of gypsophila seedlings and cuttings.

Article 11 grants a transitional period of 180 days for the National Plant Protection Organisations (NPPOs) of the countries of origin to adapt their procedures to the new requirements, specifically with regard to:

i. Seedlings of Gypsophila elegans and Gypsophila paniculata originating in Israel; and

ii. Seeds of:

  • Gypsophila elegans originating in Denmark, France, Hungary and the Netherlands;
  • Gypsophila paniculata originating in Denmark and the Netherlands; and
  • Gypsophila muralis originating in Denmark.

During this 180-day transitional period, the requirements in force on the date of entry into force of the Ordinance shall continue to apply.

title: Kiwifruit from China: biosecurity import requirements draft report
description:
The biosecurity import requirement draft report for kiwifruit from China proposes that the importation of commercially produced fresh kiwifruit (Actinidia chinensis and A. deliciosa) from all commercial production areas of China to Australia for human consumption be permitted, subject to a range of biosecurity requirements.

The report identifies pests of biosecurity concern to Australia that are potentially associated with the importation of commercially produced fresh kiwifruit from China, the risk assessments for the identified pests, and the proposed risk management measures designed to reduce biosecurity risks to an acceptable level.

description: The notified document establishes the phytosanitary requirements for the importation of in vitro Mandevilla sanderi plants originating in the United States of America.1. The shipment must be accompanied by an official phytosanitary certificate, which certifies that the plants have been officially inspected by the national plant protection organization (NPPO) of the country of origin, and indicates under "Additional declaration" that the shipment comes from a crop inspected during the growth period at an appropriate time or times for the detection of pests and is free of: Pseudomonas savastanoi pv. savastanoi.2. The shipment will be subject to phytosanitary inspection and sampling for phytosanitary diagnosis by inspectors from the Quarantine Directorate at the agricultural quarantine facility at the point of entry into the country, for the application of the phytosanitary measures.Shipments will be subject to phytosanitary checks by plant quarantine inspectors from the Institute for Agricultural and Livestock Protection and Health, who will verify compliance with the phytosanitary requirements and decide whether or not to authorize importation, on the basis of the accompanying documents.

title: Resolución 256-2026-IPSA, Establecimiento de Requisitos Fitosanitarios para la Importación de canela en raja (Cinnamomum verum), origen Viet Nam
description:
Este documento establece los requisitos fitosanitarios de importación canela en raja (Cinnamomum verum), origen Viet Nam.

 

1. El envío deberá estar acompañado de un Certificado Fitosanitario Oficial, indicando que el producto vegetal ha sido inspeccionado oficialmente por la ONPF del país de origen y encontrado libre de: Trogoderma granarium.

2. El envío será sujeto a inspección fitosanitaria y muestreo para diagnóstico fitosanitario por inspectores de la Dirección de Cuarentena, en el puesto de Cuarentena Agropecuario de ingreso al país, para la aplicación de la medida fitosanitaria.

 

Los envíos serán sometidos a control fitosanitario por los inspectores de cuarentena vegetal del Instituto de Protección y Sanidad Agropecuaria, quienes verificarán el cumplimiento de los requisitos fitosanitarios y con base a la documentación que respalda el envío, resolverán la solicitud de autorización de importación.

title: Draft of the amended Food Safety Law 2010
description:
The purpose of this addendum is to inform WTO Members that Draft of the Food Safety Law replacing the Food Safety Law 2010 (notified in G/SPS/N/VNM/187 on 3 August 2026) has been revised.

The updated draft Law only introduces amendments in the spirit of clarifying management measures and facilitating trade, such as: clearly specifying the categories of products eligible for declaration of product standards for circulation under Point b, Clause 3, Article 57 of the draft Law; simplifying the renewal procedure by requiring establishments to submit only a renewal notification, without requiring the submission of technical dossiers; further clarifying the scope of regulation and subjects of application; adding definitions of terms such as risk analysis, risk management, health supplements, supplementary foods, etc.; and supplementing and further clarifying relevant provisions.

title: Draft Commission Delegated Regulation amending Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/127 as regards the requirements on pesticides in infant formula and follow-on formula (Text with EEA relevance)
description:
This draft Commission Regulation aims to amend Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/127 by aligning the maximum residue levels for certain pesticides laid down in that Regulation for infant and follow-on formula with the most recent lower values specified for those substances in cattle milk in Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 on maximum residue levels of pesticides.

The proposed amendments to Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/127 relate to the fact that the maximum residue levels laid down in Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 for 2-amino-4-methoxy-6-(trifluormethyl)-1,3,5-triazine (AMTT), resulting from the use of tritosulfuron, carbofuran, chlordane, emamectin, endrin, epoxiconazole, fenamiphos, fluometuron, haloxyfop, oxamyl, phosmet, spirodiclofen and topramezone in cattle milk have been amended resulting in values lower than those specified by Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/127 in infant formula and follow-on formula. In order to ensure the highest level of consumer safety, it is necessary to adjust the maximum residue levels for those pesticides in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/127 to the most recent values provided for in Regulation (EC) No 396/2005. The draft Regulation foresees a grace period of 12 months.

title: Plants for Planting 155.02.06 - Adoption Date of regulation
description:
The Ministry for Primary Industries has modified the content of the previously notified draft regulation. Following feedback from domestic industry, New Zealand will not add additional phytosanitary measures originally proposed for the following host pest associations:

  • Alnus and Phytophthora alpina, P. debattistii, P. heteromorpha, P. pseudogregata
  • Amaranthus and Cucumber green mottle mosaic virus
  • Cedrus and Lecanosticta acicola
  • Corylus and Phytoplasma 16SrV–D – “Flavescence dorée”
  • Eucalyptus and Diaporthe malorum
  • Hibiscus and Tomato chlorosis virus
  • Ipomoea and Tomato chlorosis virus
  • Malva and Pepino mosaic virus, Tomato chlorosis virus
  • Moluccella and Cucumber green mottle mosaic virus
  • Oenothera and ‘Candidatus Phytoplasma solani’
  • Paeonia and Pleiocarpon algeriense
  • Pelargonium and Tomato chlorosis virus
  • Pistacia and ‘Candidatus Phytoplasma solani’
  • Salix and Phytoplasma 16SrV–D – “Flavescence dorée”

The remaining additional phytosanitary measures originally proposed have been implemented and are now in force.

Suspended import pathways for the following seven genera have also been reinstated following a review of the import requirements. The import requirements did not need to change, and they are now open for trade:

  • Actinotus
  • Aeonium
  • Astrophytum
  • Coryphantha
  • Dioscorea
  • Mammillaria
  • Portulacaria

Whilst issuing this standard, the Ministry for Primary Industries have implemented emergency measures. These will be notified under G/SPS/N/NZL/797.
